history.summary: FLAG - NOT A HINDU TEMPLE: 'Askot Musk Deer Sanctuary Temple' is a misnomer. Askot Musk Deer Sanctuary (Askot Wildlife Sanctuary) is a protected wildlife sanctuary in Pithoragarh district, Uttarakhand, near the town of Askot - keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset. Established in 1986 to conserve the endangered Himalayan musk deer (Moschus leucogaster) and its habitat, it covers 599.93 sq km with altitudes from 600 m to 6,905 m, bounded by the Kali river (India-Nepal border) in the east and West Almora Forest Division to the west. In December 2021 the Union Environment Ministry declared it an Eco-Sensitive Zone, reducing the notified area to 454.65 sq km. Fauna includes snow leopard, Himalayan black bear, brown bear, leopard, jungle cat, Himalayan tahr, serow, goral, barking deer and high-altitude birds such as monal and snowcock. Religious places within the sanctuary include Bhanar, Chiplakot, Niirikot, Panchachuli, Kalapani and Chota Kailash (Adi Kailash); the Mallikarjun Mahadev Temple at Askot town (dedicated to Shiva and Parvati) is the nearest actual temple to the CSV name. Visitors need entry permits from the Uttarakhand Forest Department.

name: Askot Musk Deer Sanctuary Temple
town_description: Askot is a small town in Pithoragarh district on the Pithoragarh-Dharchula road, on the Kailash-Mansarovar pilgrimage route. Its name derives from 'Assi Kot' (eighty forts), many of which lie across the border in Nepal; the sanctuary named after it stretches east to the Kali river and north toward Tibet, with views of the Panchachuli, Neodhura and Naukana peaks.

travel.airport: Naini Saini Airport, Pithoragarh (~60 km) has limited connectivity; Pantnagar Airport is the major airport gateway
travel.railway: Tanakpur railway station, about 204 km away (euttaranchal)
travel.road: About 54 km from Pithoragarh on the Pithoragarh-Dharchula highway, about 117 km from Almora; reachable via Haldwani-Almora or Tanakpur-Pithoragarh routes

visitor_information.best_time: April to June and September to November (multiple sources agree)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daylight hours recommended (sunrise to sunset); entry permits from the Uttarakhand Forest Department are required - confirm current timings locally
